title: The Symmetric Budget
root_cause: Two independent P_yz asymmetry sources in apply_gamma_311_recursive: (1) _bbox_hash_payload uses absolute lo,hi coords -- payload bytes differ under P_yz; (2) for N > d_A, _orthogonal_decompose(parent.stalk, N) uses Sector B/C dims -- child Sector A masses depend on absolute position/normal stalks, which are P_yz-variant.
fix_1_formula: SHA256(pack(>ddd, ex, ey, ez) + pack(>I, depth) + pack(>I, index))[:16]
fix_1_invariance: extents are P_yz-invariant under any coordinate reflection
fix_2_rule: stalk_A_i = stalk_A / N for all i (uniform equal split)
fix_2_invariance: equal Sector A mass per child -> mass-weighted centroid = geometric centroid of bbox -> P_yz-covariant focal point evolution -> P_yz-invariant LOD values at every recursion depth
wraps_g_inject: apply_gamma_312 reimplements the partition kernel with both fixes, then applies EXP-311 G_inject EMA
fork_a_assertions: G_inject_log non-empty, all C entries non-zero
fork_b_upgrade: EXP-311 Fork B was single-step only; EXP-312 Fork B upgrades to full multi-step P_yz invariance
k_bound_note: K_bound (len(zlib.compress(payload))) is empirically equal (24 bytes) for any 16-char hex payload; the K_bound asymmetry was misidentified -- actual mechanism is Sector A decompose coupling into Sector B/C dims
fix_2_replaces: zero-padding approach (_stalk_A_decompose_312) rejected: non-uniform index-based mass assignment couples to octant spatial ordering which permutes under P_yz (index i <-> i XOR 4), breaking focal point covariance
